sources.name: bengio03a.pdf
sources.locator: JMLR 3 (2003), pp.1138–1142, §1 n-gram conditional probability and §2 A Neural Model, Figure 1
sources.inspection_note: n-gram uses last n−1 symbols; §2 maps each vocabulary ID to a shared feature vector, concatenates fixed preceding positions, then applies a tanh hidden layer and softmax output. The paper also states parameter count grows linearly in order n. This supports architectural roles and cost confounding, not a quality guarantee for the tiny Chinese data.
sources.small_excerpt: associate with each word in the vocabulary a distributed word feature vector

sources.name: torch-sparse.py
sources.inspection_note: Embedding dictionary rows have shape (num_embeddings, embedding_dim), input indices retrieve corresponding feature vectors. No max_norm renormalization is used by this project.
sources.small_excerpt: weight (Tensor): the learnable weights of the module of shape (num_embeddings, embedding_dim)

sources.name: torch-linear.py
sources.inspection_note: Linear has weight shape (out_features, in_features) plus out_features bias by default, establishing the MLP width and parameter formula.
sources.small_excerpt: Applies an affine linear transformation to the incoming data

sources.name: torch-functional.py
sources.inspection_note: Read the actual 2.14.1 source signature: reduction=mean, ignore_index=-100, label_smoothing=0.0; class-index targets mean over targets. Here no target is ignored, including each EOS boundary.

sources.name: torch-adamw.py
sources.inspection_note: AdamW uses the Adam implementation with decoupled weight decay. The script only mutates parameters when the step branch is taken.

sources.name: torch-adam.py
sources.inspection_note: Read parameter/gradient collection and call to adam inside step; distinguishes backward gradients from optimizer mutation.

sources.name: torch-optimizer.py
sources.inspection_note: zero_grad resets gradient tensors; it does not itself perform an update. Own spy observes zero step calls and unchanged parameters in dry-run.
sources.small_excerpt: Reset the gradients of all optimized

necessary_context.training_introduction: Read only the frozen parent introduction to check global terminal/root/.venv path preconditions for T.3. It explicitly maps .venv/bin/python to .\.venv\Scripts\python.exe on Windows; not a whole training review.
necessary_context.scope: Only linked necessary excerpts; their old pass or author conclusions are not evidence.

derivations.parameter_count: For V=17, W=16, MLP has VW + CW² + W + WV + V = 577+256C parameters. C=1,3,5 gives 833,1345,1857. Bigram has V²=289. This is a parameter-count relation, not measured computation speed.
derivations.byte_example: ByteTokenizer has 8 specials. ASCII/UTF-8 A is byte65; 65+8=73. EOS is special2. [73,2] contains2 newly generated IDs and decodes to A; 2<32.
derivations.loss_difference: With after−before, a negative result is exactly the definition of a smaller observed loss. Example2.0−3.0=−1.0. If validation after>before while training after<before, only the observed training average improved; this alone does not establish population generalization.
